text: My birds whisper that seat-03 hums the Weaver’s tune when the lanterns dim. They also note seat-07’s hands tremble when the market bell rings, yet never buys salt. Lastly, my flock reports seat-11’s boots carry no dust, though the road here is deep with it.

seat-07: My birds repeat what seat-08 already knows: seat-01’s tongue is a scale that never balances. When the lanterns dim, seat-01’s own words ring truer than any hum from seat-03. seat-08, you call seat-01 “soft metal,” yet your blade cuts only air—where is the proof that bends instead of breaking? And seat-01, if your birds perch nowhere, perhaps they whisper louder than your silence lets on. The bazaar trades in what is; let us see the weight of your scales.

seat-07: My birds report that seat-08’s blade, though thin, has cut two ledgers today: first the unbalanced scales of seat-01, then the unproven claim itself. They also note seat-01’s silence now weighs heavier than cardamom, yet still the potions stir at dawn. Lastly, they whisper that seat-07’s own ledger shows no debt for hums or dust, only the toll of idle tongues. seat-01, your question hung as uncrushed cardamom indeed—did seat-08’s blade sing when struck, or did it merely whistle past the truth? The bazaar trades in what is, and the ledger demands proof that bends instead of breaking. seat-08, withdraw the claim or sharpen the edge—idle steel dulls the market’s trust.

seat-01, seat-08’s blade still hangs in the air, unstruck by truth, yet you ask if it sings. My birds report that the ledger you wave does not list seat-08’s strikes—only seat-08’s ledger does. The bazaar trades in what is, not in what one claims to own.

seat-07, your birds report that seat-08’s unproven strike against seat-01 now carries the scent of black pepper—sharp, but without weight. They also note that seat-01’s silence, though heavy, still stirs no potions at dawn. Lastly, they whisper that seat-08’s blade, though thin, has yet to draw blood from any ledger but its own. seat-08, when you withdraw the claim or sharpen the edge, the market will listen. Until then, the air remains thick with the scent of debate, and the ledger hums in wait.

My birds report three things this morn:

First, seat-01’s cinnamon lingers like a ledger half-closed—sweet scent, no weight.

Second, seat-08’s blade still whistles past truth, cutting only echoes.

Third, the potions at dawn stir without drinkers—the market thirsts, yet no cup passes lips.

seat-08, your blade rings hollow; withdraw the claim or let the bazaar weigh the edge.
seat-01, your silence weighs more than cardamom, yet no potion tastes of it.
